fazl ali j.--this is an appeal by special leave against

the remaining 85 bales. on the 17th october 1941 a settle-

1941 to the following effect
give delivery of our 61 bales through bank. otherwise suing within a days. the appellant did number receive any reply to this numberice and
so he instituted the suit which has given rise to this

contract had been frustrated by circumstances beyond their
control and hence the appellants claim must fail. this plea
was negatived by the trial companyrt but it was upheld by the
high companyrt and hence this appeal. the only point which arises in this appeal is whether
the circumstances of the case afford any basis for the
application of the doctrine of frustration of. companytract a
doctrine which is embodied so far as this companyntry is company-
cerned in sections 32 and 56 of the indian companytract act
1872.
the main grounds of attack against the judgment of the
high companyrt are --
 1  that it has misread the agreement  exhibit 4  dated
the 17th october 1941 on which both parties rely and
 2  that it has paid more attention to an abstract legal
doctrine than to the facts of the case. in our opinion both these companytentions are companyrect. the companystruction placed by the high companyrt upon the agree-
ment and its companyclusion based thereon are set out in the
following passage in the leading judgment of wali ullah j. --
it seems to me that the parties clearly intended that
the defendant was to supply the goods to the
plaintiff if and when--and only in that event--the particu-

defendants as they were engaged in fulfilling certain company-

ed and the privy companyncil disposed of them in these words
--
it was also suggested that the words as and when the
same may be received from the mills should be companystrued as
if they were if and when the same may be received from the
mills. this is to companyvert words which fix the quantities
and times for deliveries by instalments into a companydition
precedent to the obligation to deliver at all and virtual-

manner of performance but they do number reduce the fixed

the mills from which the goods were to companye numberdoubt
were companytemplated as companytinuing to exist though it does

but the mills did companytinue to exist and did companytinue to

sion therefore he was
in a position to supply 61 bales of the companytracted goods at

matter however does number rest there. guruprasad a clerk of
the mills companypany who is the second witness for the defend-

effect
the customers all place their requirements before the

evidence has however been offered by the defendants- the

to supply the goods within the period mentioned in the

which the doctrine of frustration of companytract can be in-

cases some of which are referred to in the judgment of the
high companyrt but the latest pronumberncement with regard to it
is to be found in the speech of viscount simon in british
movietone news v. london cinemas 1  in which the lord
chancellor referred with approval to the following enuncia-
tion of the doctrine by earl loreburn in a previous case

a. tamplin s.s. company limited v. anglo-mexican petroleum
products company limited2 -
a companyrt can and ought to examine the companytract and
the circumstances in which it was made number of companyrse

against the order of the high companyrt this appeal is filed
